claims.claim_text: I exited my patrol vehicle and began approaching the vehicle on the passenger side.
The driver abruptly accelerated away from the traffic stop, making a hard-right turn across oncoming traffic.
During the pursuit, the subject collided with two civilian vehicles, causing one vehicle to overturn.
Laguna Beach Police officers successfully deployed a spike strip, which caused all four tires of the Mercedes to deflate.
My patrol unit, Officer Trujillo's unit, and Sergeant Holt's unit took positions approximately 15 feet from the stopped Mercedes.
I observed the subject remain seated in the driver's seat for approximately 30 seconds, appearing to look around the interior of the vehicle.
The subject placed his left hand behind his back and made a distinct reaching motion toward his left hip area.
I discharged my department-issued Glock 17 firearm, firing four rounds at the subject at approximately 1839 hours.
At this point, Officer Trujillo deployed his department-issued Taser, which struck the subject and caused him to fall to the ground.
I conducted a search of the subject's person and recovered a small black semi-automatic pistol from the subject's right front waistband area.
The subject reached speeds of approximately 90 miles per hour and was observed driving on the wrong side of the road and swerving into oncoming traffic.
Sergeant Holt broadcast over the radio that shots had been fired and a Taser had been deployed.
The subject survived his injuries, which included two gunshot wounds to the upper torso and one to the left forearm.
Corporal Novak successfully executed a pursuit intervention technique (PIT) maneuver, bringing the Mercedes to a stop in the southbound lane of Pacific Coast Highway.
The subject yelled profanities at the officers while continuing to make threatening gestures consistent with pointing a weapon.
